tests.note: A real convergence document round-trips its verdict exactly; every permitted verdict proven not to collapse

commands.command: node tools/sdd/cli.mjs agent scope-check --spec SPEC-0002 --session ASES-0007

environment: local developer workstation, Windows 11, Node v24.18.0
notes: Original assertion: SPEC-0002 reads back as the literal string PASS WITH ACCEPTED LIMITATIONS.

Why it became stale: the convergence re-run legitimately moved the verdict to FAIL. The test was pinned to the document rather than to the parser, so it failed for a reason unrelated to the code under test.
New invariant: the declaration is read out of the metadata row independently, and the parser must return exactly that. Every permitted verdict is additionally round-tripped.

Why it remains meaningful: it still fails the moment prefix matching returns, because PASS WITH ACCEPTED LIMITATIONS would collapse to PASS and stop matching the declaration. It no longer fails when the verdict simply changes.
No assertion was weakened to obtain green. The test now checks strictly more than before: the document round-trip plus all three verdicts.
The parser was a prohibited path for this task, so the fix could not be made by editing the code under test.
